AREA 01 OF 12

Starting out: menus, modes & saving

The start menu, worlds, creative and survival, pausing, saving and quitting.

Creative and survival modes (F4)

Available

Creative · Survival

There are exactly two modes. Press F4 any time to switch between creative and survival; your pack, hotbar and position stay as they are. New worlds always start in creative, and each world remembers the mode it was saved in.

F4
Switch creative / survival (in the world (refused while connected to a server))

Creative: instant mining, free placing/crafting, any tool, unlimited ammo, Build catalog/brushes/undo, block picking, flight, map travel, world controls and one-hit animal removal without drops. Survival: timed mining/tool advice, carry capacity, health/food/water/stamina bars, falls, R eat, T drink, X craft, read-only World tab and rest-point respawn. No difficulty presets. Targeted 35cfc2f8 update: ambient temperature has no survival effect; other mode evidence retains its original audit.

Start menu

Available

Menus

Use Continue to resume the loaded world or Worlds to choose or create one. The menu also offers Multiplayer, Structure workshop, Settings, Credits and Quit. Continue is disabled when no usable world is loaded. Use the mouse or arrow keys and Enter; Esc returns from a sub-page.

Worlds: create, play, rename, duplicate and back up

Available

Menus

Worlds lists the current save first, then starred saves and recent worlds. A click selects a row; Play world, Enter or a double-click opens it. Search, wheel scrolling and page keys browse the list. Create world offers name, seed, mode and generation. Rename, Duplicate and Create backup act on the selected save; deleting an inactive save requires a 3-second hold.

Typing / Backspace / Ctrl+Backspace
Filter world names / delete one character / clear the filter
Up / Down / Page Up / Page Down / mouse wheel
Browse saved worlds
Enter / Play world / double-click row
Open the selected world; one click only selects it
Ctrl+R / Ctrl+D / Ctrl+B
Rename / duplicate / back up the selected world
Tab / Shift+Tab
Star the selected world / toggle starred-only
Hold Delete world or Delete for 3 seconds
Delete the selected inactive world; release early to cancel
Esc / Back
Return to the start menu

Targeted 5 November 2026 source follow-up at aa136e0103ce5599c6d8a9f70c669dbc758b7357. Rename changes display metadata. Duplicate and backup preserve independent copies; active hosting and unfinished save recovery must be resolved first. Some old worlds have unknown or partial session history. Source-checked; this wiki slice ran no native game or two-computer playtest. Unrelated ledger rows retain their earlier audit.

Esc key and what pauses the game

Available

Any mode

Esc closes the current panel or dialog; with no panel open, it opens the pause menu and releases the mouse. Choose Settings there. Esc from those settings returns to the pause menu. Local worlds pause in these menus and the fullscreen map; the pack does not pause. A connected server keeps running.

Esc
Close the active layer, or open the pause menu
Esc from in-game Settings
Return to the pause menu
Resume
Return to play

Mouse capture and release

Available

Any mode

Click the world to capture the mouse; that click never mines or places. Panels, Esc, Print Screen, focus loss or covering the window release it. Returning focus does not capture it automatically. While released you cannot move or look.

Print Screen

Saving, Main menu and quitting

Available

Any mode

The world autosaves about every 30 seconds when it has unsaved changes, and F6 saves at once, showing 'World saved safely' after the file is written; a joined server world is not saved locally. Settings > Main menu saves and returns to the start menu. Ctrl+Q, Save & quit, Quit or closing the window all save first; if saving fails, the game stays open.

F6

Ctrl+Q
Save and quit (anywhere in a session)
Settings > Save & quit
Save and quit (in-game Settings)
Settings > Main menu
Save and return to the start menu (in-game Settings)
Start menu > Quit / window close button
Save and quit (start menu / anywhere)

Limited

AREA 02 OF 12

Moving, camera & screen

Walking, jumping, sneaking, crawling, swimming and flying, the camera, and what the screen shows you.

Walking and looking around

Available

Creative · Survival

Move with W A S D and look with the mouse once the pointer is captured. You walk at about 4.3 m/s, climb half-metre steps without jumping, and need to jump onto a full one-metre block.

W / A / S / D
Walk forward / left / back / right (on foot, pointer captured)
Mouse
Look around (pointer captured, no panel open)

Keys are physical positions: on AZERTY or other layouts use the key that sits where W is on a QWERTY board. Jumps mostly keep their take-off direction. Movement runs on a fixed 60 Hz tick, so speed does not depend on frame rate.

Sprinting

Available

Creative · Survival

Hold Ctrl while moving forward with W to sprint at about 5.6 m/s. A sprint-jump adds a small forward push. In survival, sprinting uses stamina and stops when stamina is nearly empty.

Ctrl + W (hold)
Sprint (on foot, not sneaking or crawling)
Ctrl + Space while sprinting
Sprint-jump with a small forward push (on foot)

Ctrl with only A, D or S held does not sprint. High speed also widens the view slightly (see camera-bob-and-speed-fov).

Sneaking (ledge guard)

Available

Creative · Survival

Hold Shift on the ground to sneak at about 1.3 m/s with a slightly lower view. While sneaking you cannot walk off an edge, and the hint under the crosshair reads 'SNEAK: LEDGE GUARD ACTIVE'.

Shift (hold)
Sneak with ledge protection (on the ground, not flying or in water)

Shift is shared: it also switches mining/placing to half-metre pieces, dives while swimming, descends while flying and steadies ranged weapons.

Crawling

Available

Creative · Survival

Press C on foot to crawl with a 0.6 m tall body at about 1 m/s to get through low gaps. Press C again or Space to stand; you only stand once there is full headroom, and in a low space the game keeps you crawling automatically.

Space

Inside a vehicle C changes camera instead. You cannot jump while crawling.

Swimming and diving

Available

Creative · Survival

Once water reaches your chest you swim. W and S follow the direction you look (look down to dive), Space swims up, Shift dives and Ctrl swims faster; with no keys you hold your depth.

Space (hold)
Swim upward (any part of the body in water)
Shift (hold)
Dive (in water)
Ctrl + W (hold)
Swim faster (swimming)

Ankle-deep wading stays upright. No drowning or air meter was found in this code (grep drown/breath/oxygen); being underwater only drains stamina slowly in survival.

Creative flight

Available

Creative

In creative, press F or double-tap Space on dry land to start or stop flying. Hold Space to rise, Shift to descend and Ctrl to boost from 16 to 32 m/s. Flight also ends when you switch to survival, board a vehicle or respawn.

Space (hold)
Rise (flying)
Shift (hold)
Descend (flying)
Ctrl (hold)
Fly at boosted speed (flying)
W / A / S / D
Fly horizontally (flying)

In survival, F only shows 'Flight is available in creative mode'. Touching the ground does not end flight.

Camera bob and speed field of view

Available

Creative · Survival

Walking gently bobs the camera; turn it off in Settings > Gameplay > Movement > Camera bob. Speed FOV widens the view by up to 5 degrees at high horizontal speed, reaching full widening at about 16 m/s; jumps and falls do not change it. Turn it off with Settings > Gameplay > Movement > Speed FOV. When you lose at least 1 HP, the camera dips briefly by up to 7 cm; Settings > Gameplay > Movement > Damage bob sets this to Off, Reduced or Full (Full by default).

Targeted settings-route check: aa136e0103ce5599c6d8a9f70c669dbc758b7357 (2026-11-05). Other numeric/visual behavior retains its earlier audit. Graphics, audio and interface preferences now follow the player (src/settings_profile.rs:25-39); this is not a fresh capture or play test.

HUD overview

Available

Creative · Survival

During play the status line sits top-left, the looking-at card top-right just left of the compact map, the compact map top-right with the FPS/coordinates box beneath it, the crosshair and action hint in the middle, the four survival bars lower-left (survival only) and the ten-slot hotbar with its item label at the bottom.

Crosshair and aiming reticle

Available

Creative · Survival

A small plus-shaped crosshair marks your aim. It inverts the colours beneath it so it stays readable over sky, grass or stone. With a bow, rifle or throwable, its four lines spread apart as your accuracy drops and close back into a plus as your aim steadies.

Changed after the audited commit dd29d91: game commit 10d7ea4 (on main) replaced the orange-to-green dotted ring and green target tint with the spreading inverted crosshair. Aircraft gun pipper rings are separate and not covered here.

Available

Creative · Survival

When you aim at a block within 6 m, a card at the top right, just left of the compact map, shows its 3D icon, name, distance and mining advice ('CREATIVE INSTANT BREAK', a recommended tool, or 'NO SPECIAL TOOL NEEDED'). Status line, pickup and damage feedback

Available

Creative · Survival

Actions report in the top-left status line, for example 'Collected <block> x<pieces>', 'Capacity full; block left behind' or 'Inventory opened'. Survival: needs, health & home

Health, hunger, thirst and stamina, dangers, death and respawn, and the home crate.

Health, hunger, thirst and stamina

Available

Survival

Survival shows four bars: HP, HUNGER, THIRST and STAMINA (0-100). A full hunger bar lasts about 40 minutes and a full thirst bar about 30 minutes; health slowly regenerates while both stay above 65.

Ctrl + W
Sprint (uses stamina; needs more than 3%) (on foot or swimming)

Meters do not change in creative. There is no drowning: being underwater only slows stamina recovery.

Fall damage and other dangers

Available

Survival

Falls of up to 3 m are free; each extra metre costs 5 HP, so about 23 m is fatal from full health. Animals never attack; besides falls, starvation, thirst and explosions hurt you. Ambient cold and heat do not cause damage.

No drowning, lava, fire, cactus or hostile-mob damage exists in this snapshot. Fall damage only applies when landing on solid ground. Targeted policy update at 35cfc2f8: survival.rs tick no longer applies temperature damage; existing fall/animal evidence retains its original audit. Death and respawn

Available

Survival

At 0 HP the 'You died' screen shows the cause and respawn location. Click Respawn or press Enter when ready. You keep your inventory and return to your rest point, with a safe nearby fallback if it is blocked or flooded.

Enter / click Respawn
Confirm respawn from the death screen

The initial rest point is the world start; establishing a home alone does not move it. Rest / set respawn changes it. Respawning grants no new starter supplies. Home crate: establish, storage, repair, pack up

Available

Creative · Survival

In the Home tab, Establish home while standing on dry, solid ground: it costs 8 board pieces (free in Creative) and places a small crate 1.5 m beside you. The crate stores up to 400 capacity while you are within 6 m. On a server only the world's saved owner has a Home; establish, repair, storage, rest and Pack up wait for server confirmation, in Survival and Creative.

Click Establish home
Place the crate (or repair a lost one at its original spot) (Home tab)
Click Establish / repair or Repair crate
Server version of the same button: 8 boards in Survival, free in Creative (Home tab, on a server)
Click a carried / stored row
Move one item into / out of storage (Home tab, within 6 m of the crate)
Shift+click a row
Move as many as fit (Home tab)
Arrow keys
Move between the three buttons and the carried and stored lists; Up from the first row returns to the buttons (Home tab)
Page Up / Page Down
Turn the page of the selected list (Home tab)
Enter / Space
Use the selected button or move one of the selected item; with Shift, move as many as fit (Home tab)
Click Pack up
Remove the crate; Survival refunds 8 Alder boards, Creative none (Home tab, storage empty)

Source-checked on 2026-11-08 at Voxelgame dfeb362ddeca56ff5de77fa26ccdb6e37d05192c; no new play test. One home at a time; to move it, empty storage and Pack up. A destroyed crate keeps its items; Establish home within 6 m of the old spot repairs it if the spot is dry, solid underneath and clear of you, otherwise nothing is used up. Pack up refunds Alder boards whatever species paid. Your rest point stays. On a server the crate also needs build permission on its plot, and other players are refused. Creative crate work earns no Home milestone.

Resting and setting your respawn point

Available

Creative · Survival

Home tab > Rest / set respawn works within 6 m of your crate, on dry ground, under a roof with cover on at least two sides. It sets your respawn point there and refills stamina, but does not heal or feed you. On a server the saved owner can rest in Survival or Creative; wait for 'Rested at Home | respawn point set'.

Source-checked on 2026-11-08 at Voxelgame dfeb362ddeca56ff5de77fa26ccdb6e37d05192c; no new play test. Leaves and tree trunks count as solid cover; plants and water do not. The shelter check runs when you press Rest. Shelter gives no warmth. Creative rest on a server, for the host or the saved owner, sets the respawn point and stamina but earns no Rested milestone. Bed rest is separate and never moves the respawn point.

Ten-slot hotbar

The hotbar has ten slots that you bind to item kinds; they start empty. Bind by hovering an item and pressing a number key, or by dragging; select slots with 1-9 and 0, the mouse wheel, or [ and ].

Slots are bindings, not containers: the count is everything of that kind in the pack. Bindings are saved with the world. Selecting a block slot puts away any tool, since an equipped tool blocks placement. With an empty slot selected the label reads 'EMPTY HANDS | E OPEN INVENTORY'.

Available

Creative · Survival

Open the inventory and choose Craft. Survival crafting queue

Available

Survival

In Survival every craft is an order in a short queue: each order takes 0.8 s, up to 8 can wait, and materials stay in the pack until an order finishes. An order that can no longer be paid for or stored waits without partial spending. Progress shows in the Craft panel and during play. The queue keeps running with the inventory closed, stops while menus or the fullscreen map are open, and is not saved. On servers each finished order waits for the server.

Enter or C, or click Queue
Add one batch as an order (Craft tab, Survival)
Confirm all
Add the reviewed batches as one order (Craft tab, Survival)
Stop queue
Clear every queued order; nothing unfinished is spent (Craft tab, while orders wait)

Source-checked on 2026-11-08 at Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480; no new play test. Messages: 'Queued <recipe> x<n> | materials kept until finished', 'Cannot queue <recipe> | check materials and carry capacity', 'Craft queue full (8 orders) | finish or cancel in Craft', 'Craft waiting | restore materials or pack space, or cancel in Craft', 'Craft queue cancelled | all unspent materials kept'. Switching to Creative empties the queue. On servers Home and furniture storage also wait while orders are queued. The queue arrived in game commit 23b2f021 (17 October 2026).

Mining and collecting blocks

Available

Creative · Survival

Hold left click on a block within 6 m. In survival a progress bar fills, then the whole 1 m block (up to 8 pieces) goes straight into your pack; hold Shift to take a single half-metre piece. Nothing drops on the ground: if the pieces do not fit, the block stays put.

Hold left click
Mine the targeted block (survival) / remove it instantly (creative) (on foot, aiming within 6 m)
Shift + hold left click
Mine a single half-metre piece (detail brush) (on foot)

Source-checked on 2026-11-08 at Voxelgame dfeb362ddeca56ff5de77fa26ccdb6e37d05192c; no new play test. If furniture stands between you and the block, holding left click stops with 'Furniture blocks that mining target' and nothing is mined. Gaps between furniture parts and blocks nearer than the furniture still work. Water and other liquids cannot be collected. Creative mining collects nothing and can be undone. Feedback is a status-line message and flying chips; in survival, cracks also grow on the block in 8 stages, and gains show in the lower-right collection feed.

Mining speed and tool effectiveness

Available

Survival

Any block can be mined by hand; a tool only speeds up its own material class. Pickaxe x4 on rock, crystal, glass, ice and masonry; hatchet x3.6 on logs, boards, leaves and other wooden blocks; shovel x3.4 on loose ground.

The time is for the whole targeted 1 m block; detail (Shift) mining takes the same time for one piece. Fallen petals and Fallen leaves are plants that a shovel speeds up; Bamboo and Date clusters are plants a hatchet speeds up.

Felling trees

Available

Creative · Survival

Cutting a log on a natural tree (or a cactus) brings down that piece and everything growing from it. In survival the chop takes the combined time of all removed wood and leaves, and all of it goes into your pack.

Cutting the root removes the whole tree; cutting a branch keeps the trunk below. If the whole harvest does not fit you get 'Need X capacity free to collect this connected tree' and nothing is cut. Logs you placed yourself mine like ordinary blocks. Status shows 'Felled a tree: N <log> and M <leaves>'.

Stone tools (single tier, no durability)

Available

Creative · Survival

There is one tool tier: Stone sword, Stone pickaxe, Stone hatchet and Stone shovel. Tools never wear out or break.

No wooden or iron tier exists. The Stone sword has no mining bonus. Bow, rifle, throwing rocks and dynamite are covered by the combat audit; their recipes are in crafting-recipes.

Where crafting materials come from

Available

Survival

Natural stone and wood are everywhere; Sand and Clay line shores, Reeds grow in wetlands, Wild flax (for fiber) grows in meadows of new worlds, and feathers, wool and meat come from animals.

Biome placement detail belongs to the world audit; this list only links recipe inputs to known sources. Older (generation-9) worlds have no Wild flax, so use Wool for bindings there. Glow crystal does not generate naturally, but no recipe needs it (see lumen-crystal-supply).

Block types and material families

Available

Creative · Survival

The Blocks catalog lists 286 block types you can hold, including 6 kinds of water, boards from 15 kinds of wood and 92 doors in three styles. Metals and gems are limited to decorative stone blocks: Iron ore, Bog iron, Red rock, Amethyst and Glow crystal.

Iron ore and Bog iron can be mined and placed but have no recipe or smelting use. No copper, tin, bronze, gold, platinum, diamond or marble exists. Blocks with no survival source: Amethyst cluster (creative only), Green roof tile (creative), Home crate (Home tab only). Pink options are natural: Pink blossom leaves, Fallen petals, Fireweed, Polished granite (pink-gray). Items on the ground and manual dropping

Available

Survival

In survival, J drops one selected carried item and Ctrl+J drops everything of that kind. With Pack open, point at its icon first. Approach an unobstructed dropped stack after its short pickup delay to collect what fits; the remainder stays on the ground.

J
Drop one selected carried item, or the hovered Pack item (survival; default binding)
Ctrl+J
Drop the whole carried quantity of that item kind (survival; default bindings)
Approach a dropped item
Collect the amount that fits after the pickup delay

A blocked launch or a full ground-item pool keeps the carried items and explains the refusal. Dragging off the Pack does not drop items; dragging a hotbar slot off the bar only clears its binding. There is no manual stack-splitting control. Inventory remains under active development. Targeted source review on 5 November 2026 at Voxelgame aa136e0103ce5599c6d8a9f70c669dbc758b7357. Source tests were read, not run; no native play test is claimed.

Building & creative tools

Placing blocks, half-metre detail, creative brushes, undo, palettes and explosives for clearing ground.

Wooden doors

Available

Creative · Survival

Craftable doors in Plain, Panelled and Windowed styles, in fifteen exact woods or any boards, and two sizes: 1 x 2 m with one leaf or 2 x 3 m with two. Right click hangs one on solid ground and opens or closes it; mining a leaf takes the whole door down. In Creative, Shift + left click moves a complete closed door as one undoable step.

Right click with a door held
Hang it on solid ground (needs free space)
Right click a hung door
Open or close it
Left click a door leaf (hold in Survival)
Take the whole door down
Shift + Left click a closed door (Creative)
Lock it to move: R turns, right click places, left click or B cancels
Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z after a door move
Undo or redo the move (Creative, also on a server)

Source-checked on 2026-11-08 at Voxelgame dfeb362ddeca56ff5de77fa26ccdb6e37d05192c; no new play test. Adds three styles, fifteen exact woods and Creative door moves (see door-styles-and-moves). Corrects the 5 November note: on a server, Survival take-down goes through server mining, which returns the exact door of any wood, so the client's "Wood-specific doors can only be taken down in Creative on servers" message is not reached in normal play. Blueprints skip door leaves.

Door styles, woods and moves

Available

Creative · Survival

E > Craft shows Style, Wood and Size buttons on any door recipe. Plain and Panelled cost one block of the chosen boards (two for wide); Windowed costs 6 board and 2 glass pieces (12 and 4 for wide). E > Craft > a door recipe > Style / Wood / Size
Step to the next style, wood or size; the other choices stay

Furniture and carpentry

Available

Creative · Survival

Thirty-one reusable plans build seats, four table sizes, kitchen units, bathroom fixtures, a cooking stove, storage furniture, beds and lamps. Survival carpentry needs a carried Furniture hammer: choose the materials, read the Need / have counts and pay only when the piece is placed. Creative is free. Blocks and mining aimed at furniture are refused.

E with a plan selected or the hammer in hand
Open the carpentry workbench; aim at placed furniture to change its materials
R / Right click
Turn the furniture ghost 90 degrees / place it
Left click, with a plan selected
Take up the aimed furniture; empty its storage first
Shift + Left click, with a plan selected
Lock the aimed furniture to move it: R turns, right click places, left click cancels
Shift + Right click
Place a floor kitchen piece against the side of the aimed one
Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z
Undo / redo the last furniture step
B
Put the furniture tool away
Right click a seat / Space or Right click while seated
Sit nearby with the plan put away / stand when the exit is clear
Right click a block or hold left click at furniture
Refused: "Furniture blocks that placement" / "Furniture blocks that mining target"

Source-checked on 2026-11-08 at Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480; no new play test. Beds, wardrobes and joining tables now exist, replacing the old missing-furniture claim. Sizes stay fixed; the Standard size control is disabled. Basins store no water. On a server, furniture waits for the server to confirm each action. The coffee and side table plan tooltips now say they hold a red lantern, as the code does. Storage, beds and lamps are only summarised in this guide.

Moving, changing materials and furniture Undo

Available

Creative · Survival

With a plan selected, Shift+left click locks a piece to move it, R turns the ghost and right click places it; left click takes it up and returns only paid materials when the pack has room. Available

Creative · Survival

A one-metre board chest from one block of any boards. Chest refinishing

Available

Creative · Survival

With the Furniture hammer, press E or right click at a placed wooden chest to open Refinish chest. Choose Body, Lid and Fittings woods, then Apply changes; contents stay. Survival pays 4 body, 3 lid and 1 fittings board; Creative is free. Ctrl+Z restores the original chest and Ctrl+Shift+Z reapplies. The Chest plan makes the same chest from a carried one. Works offline and on servers.

Placing blocks

Available

Creative · Survival

Select a block and right click to place a full 1 m cube (eight half-metre pieces) in the cell beside the face you aim at. Creative placement is free; in survival each whole block spends 8 carried pieces of that material.

Right click
Place the held block at the ghost (one block per click) (block selected, no tool equipped)

Plants and water in the target cell are overwritten; plants are not collected (code reading). If any part of the 1 m cell is occupied the whole block is refused (red outline); hold Shift to place half-metre pieces instead. Status messages: 'Cannot place a block inside the player', 'That space is already occupied', 'Need 8 <block> pieces to place a block (N carried)'. In creative, fill quick slots from E > Build or a palette preset.

Building in and under water

Available

Creative · Survival

Your aim passes through water to the first solid block, so you can target the lake or sea bed and build up from it. Water, like air and plants, counts as free space and is replaced by placed blocks; you cannot click the water surface itself.

To bridge water, build out from the shore or up from the bed. Water flow belongs to the world/water pages.

Available

Creative

Hold Shift on the first click
Build in half-metre steps instead of whole blocks (creative)

If a cell holds a solid block nothing is built, except with Replace, which only swaps the material you aim at. Water and plants do not block a build. Line, Wall and Floor corners are ghost positions (where a block would go), unlike Copy and Replace, which use the blocks you aim at.

Undo and redo building

Available

Creative

In creative, Ctrl+Z undoes and Ctrl+Shift+Z redoes your building in this session: brush actions, blueprints, single blocks placed, and blocks or trees mined. Door moves, chest refinishing and furniture steps share the same history, so the newest step is undone first; at most 32 steps are kept. Undo changes nothing if those cells were altered since or if it would put a block inside you, and it stops at the save edit limit.

Ctrl+Z
Undo the newest step (creative)
Ctrl+Shift+Z
Redo (creative)
Undo / Redo buttons
Same as the keys (E > Build, creative)

Source-checked on 2026-11-08 at Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480; no new play test. Survival block edits and explosions are not recorded; in survival Ctrl+Z reaches only furniture and chest-refinishing steps. Door moves are Creative only. On a server, Undo and Redo of door moves, chest refinishing and furniture wait for the server. History is session-only; empty history reports "No building history in this session".

TNT: place and ignite (G)

Available

Creative · Survival

Place TNT like any block; a whole block holds 8 charges and a Shift-placed half-metre piece holds 1. Aim at it and press G: it and every TNT piece touching it (even diagonally) light together on a 2.6-second fuse, pop loose, and can fall, roll or float before exploding.

G
Ignite the aimed TNT and all TNT touching it (aiming at TNT within 6 m; on a server, after the server confirms)
Right click
Place TNT (Shift: one half-metre charge) (TNT selected)
Left click
Mine TNT back without setting it off (any)

Source-checked on 2026-11-08 at Voxelgame dfeb362ddeca56ff5de77fa26ccdb6e37d05192c; no new play test. On multiplayer servers G asks the server to light the TNT; the old 'Explosives aren't available on servers yet' refusal no longer applies. The server reports the result, and lit TNT on a server is lost if the server restarts. In survival TNT is crafted and a whole block spends 8 pieces. Pressing G on one whole block reports an '8-charge TNT cluster' because each block counts as 8 half-metre charges. Lit charges are not saved: quitting while a fuse burns loses that TNT.

Explosions: reach, damage and terrain

Available

Creative · Survival

One whole TNT block blasts about 4.25 m; touching groups explode as one bigger blast (up to 10.5 m), while a single half-metre charge or dynamite stick reaches only about 1.5 m. Survival players near a blast lose health and are knocked back (creative players are unharmed), creatures are hurt in both modes, and blasted blocks are destroyed, not collected.

Derived from the formulas: one whole TNT block cannot break obsidian (strength at most 4.25 + 0.55 < 5.0), and solid rock gives way only close to the charge. Values marked 'about' are computed from code constants, not measured in play. The cleared count in the status line is in half-metre voxels. Explosions are not undoable.

Throwing dynamite

Available

Creative · Survival

Select dynamite, hold right click to wind up and release to throw; a longer wind-up throws farther. The fuse starts on release and the stick goes off 2.3 s later where it stops, sticking to the first surface it hits (walls and ceilings included), as a small fixed blast of about 1.5 m.

Right click (hold, then release)
Wind up and throw a dynamite stick (dynamite selected)

Source-checked on 2026-11-08 at Voxelgame dfeb362ddeca56ff5de77fa26ccdb6e37d05192c; no new play test. Works on multiplayer servers: releasing sends a request, the server throws the stick and, in Survival, spends one; a refused throw keeps the stick. The old 'Explosives aren't available on servers yet' refusal no longer applies to dynamite. Burning dynamite on a server is lost if the server restarts. Creative throws are unlimited; survival spends one stick per throw. You cannot place blocks while dynamite is in hand. Opening a menu cancels a wind-up.

World generations (terrain rule versions)

Available

Any mode

Each world keeps its saved terrain generation. Create world defaults to generation 12 and allows earlier preserved generations. Loading an existing save restores its generation instead of upgrading its terrain rules.

Choose and view a world seed

Available

Menus

Create world accepts an unsigned decimal seed, or a blank field for a fresh seed. Choose the same seed and terrain generation to use the same procedural rules. Worlds shows the selected save’s seed when its header can be read.

Targeted 5 November 2026 source follow-up at aa136e0103ce5599c6d8a9f70c669dbc758b7357. Valid seed range is 0–18446744073709551615. A fresh seed is resolved only on confirmation; Cancel creates no world. A matching seed alone does not promise matching terrain across different generations. 92 biomes

Available

Any mode

Worlds contain 92 named biomes, from meadows, orchards and bamboo thickets to salt flats, kelp forests, meteor fields and surface lava tubes. All 92 can generate naturally, and the map locator can find any of them.

You can read your current biome on the FPS-and-coordinates readout (see position-readout) or in the status message after map travel.

Endless archipelago and the starting island

Available

Any mode

The world is an endless sea of island groups. You start at X 0, Z 0 on a large island several kilometres across, in a protected, gentle meadow clearing. Other islands range from small islets and palm-ringed atolls to large islands and occasional continent-sized landmasses. Open ocean separates island groups, and satellite islets sit at least 240 m offshore.

The size figures are internal envelope values, not measured coastline lengths, so the wiki should say only 'several kilometres across'. The starting island keeps its size in every generation (archipelago.rs:159-163). Coordinates: north is -Z, south is +Z and east is +X.

Hillside caves

Available

Any mode

Some hills have cave entrances that lead into one of three layouts: branching passages around a chamber, a looping gallery around a central rock mass, or a broad vaulted hall held up by four rock pillars. Floors climb in walkable half-metre steps. Caves are single, bounded sites rather than deep cave networks.

Caves do not appear on the map. There are no stalactites, dripstone, ores or lights inside caves.

Landmarks: meteor craters, amethyst gorges, lava tubes and other geological…

Available

Any mode

Rare large sites appear across the world. Impact fields have a main crater bowl with a raised ejecta rim plus two smaller craters. Amethyst gorges are winding canyons through crystal-studded rock. On volcanic islands, cooled lava tubes are walkable roofed passages with two open skylights. Other sites include hot-spring terraces, geyser basins, oases, tepui mesas, ice spires, granite domes, karst towers, moraines and limestone pavements.

Meteor craters appear only where the site is not volcanic. Lava tubes appear only on volcanic ground. Generation-1 worlds have no impact, gorge or lava-tube sites.

Volcanoes and volcanic terrain

Available

Any mode

Some islands carry shield volcanoes, steep stratovolcanoes or breached calderas. Older ones are eroded and overgrown. Volcanic ground has basalt, obsidian, ash, lava rock, pahoehoe and glowing magma stone, and nearby geothermal areas have warm and boiling pools and steam vents. Everything is solid and cooled: there is no molten lava, and nothing burns.

No code damages players from magma stone, boiling water or steam vents (grep for MAGMA_STONE/BOILING_WATER/STEAM_VENT outside generation and rendering finds no gameplay use). Steam vents are static blocks with no steam particles.

Rivers, lakes and wetlands

Available

Any mode

Islands have river channels, inland lakes up to 62 m above sea level, marshes, bogs, mangroves, bayous and frozen lakes. All natural water is still: rivers do not flow or push you. The kind of water depends on the place: ocean water, fresh water in lakes and rivers, black water in warm wetlands, warm or boiling mineral water at hot springs, dark fjord water, and ice on frozen lakes.

Expedition sites and one-time supply finds

Available

Creative · Survival

Generation-10 worlds have three small landmarks in squares about 240 m wide, centred about 215, 340 and 440 m from spawn: the Survey workshop to the east, the Reed refuge to the south-west and the Stone overlook to the north-east. Click one in the Journal to make it your destination. Walk to within 12 m of it on foot to discover it, then press Find in the Journal while still nearby to collect its one-time supplies.

E, then Tab to Journal (or the Journal button on the…
Open the Journal with the three expedition sites listed ('?' undiscovered, '+' discovered) (in the world)
Click a site name
Make it your destination (map marker, light beacon and on-screen marker) (Journal)
Find button
Collect the site's supplies; it shows 'Taken' afterwards (Journal, within 12 m of a discovered site, on foot)

If no dry, level spot is found near a site's base position, that site is skipped, so a world can have fewer than three. The site buildings are regenerated each session and do not show on the map, but any blocks you mine or place there are kept. Without enough pack space the game says 'Leave pack space; the find will wait here'. You can still harvest the site's blocks after taking the find. The Reed refuge has a small fresh-water pool, the workshop has a glass block and carved-stone floor, and the overlook has a Glow crystal light (exploration.rs:192-242).

Day and night

Available

Creative · Survival

A full day and night lasts 20 real minutes: the sun is up for about 10 minutes and down for about 10. New worlds start about a minute after sunrise. Night is darker, with the moon and, on clear nights, stars; cows, sheep, pigs and chickens rest at night. Nothing dangerous happens at night, and neither beds nor Home rest pass time or skip the night. Time of day is saved with the world, and a server shares one clock with everyone.

Source-checked on 2026-11-08 at Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480; no new play test. Settings includes the pause menu, so local play pauses the clock there too; a server's clock keeps running. Time of day is saved with the world (save/write.rs:349).

Automatic weather

Available

Creative · Survival

Weather follows a fixed 30-minute pattern: clear, cloudy, rain, cloudy, partly cloudy, foggy, cloudy, rainstorm, thunderstorm, cloudy, 3 minutes each, blending over several seconds. Each world starts at a different point, and the whole world shares it, so rain falls over deserts too; there is no snowfall. Rain stops at the first solid or liquid block, sounds softer under a roof and stops by 1,600 metres. Thunderstorms flash lightning about every 18 seconds, with thunder after; lightning causes no damage or fires. Weather sets the sailing wind and never harms the player.

Source-checked on 2026-11-08 at Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480; no new play test. Weather values are used only by the sky, lighting, rain, sound, music and wind; survival, animals, fishing and the world never read them. Cloud bases 1,200 / 1,800 / 2,500 m and the 1,600 m rain ceiling still match the 15 October 2026 native captures at Voxelgame 61a4257; those were not repeated.

Seasons

Limited

Creative · Survival

A year is 80 real minutes, 20 minutes per season, and new worlds start in mid-summer. Seasons tint grass, broadleaf leaves, needles, blossoms, water, sky and sunlight, for example russet and gold autumn foliage and a cooler, weaker winter light. In autumn, falling leaves drift from broadleaf trees when a shader is on and Reduce motion is off; no blocks change. Seasonal leaf thinning and snow appearance remain planned. Seasons change appearance only, with no survival penalties or world-content changes.

Source-checked on 2026-11-08 at Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480; no new play test. Outside rendering, the season is read only for autumn falling leaves; world generation, animals and crafting never read it. The wiki must not claim that leaves thin or grass turns snowy until those ship. No season images exist.

Compact map

Available

Creative · Survival

A small north-up terrain map sits in the top-right corner and is on by default. It shows 128 m around you with your heading arrow, saved places, your destination and any locator highlight. Press M to hide or show it.

M

The terrain moves in 4 m jumps because the view snaps to the sample spacing (map.rs:126-134). Like the fullscreen map, it shows only generated terrain: your builds and dug or blasted ground do not appear.

Available

Creative · Survival

The panel left of the fullscreen map lists Volcano, Cliff island and Mountain range, then all 92 biomes alphabetically. Type to filter the list, then click a result or press Enter. The search spirals outward from the map centre, recentres and zooms the map on the first match, highlights matching terrain in cyan and drops a pin with distance and coordinates. It never moves you.

The search starts from the map centre, not from you, so pan the map first to search somewhere else. In survival the locator still reveals everything, because there is no fog of war. The highlight and pin stay on the compact map until you press Clear.

Available

Water & sailing

Flowing water, splashes and the small sailing boat.

Launching and packing up a sailing boat

Available

Creative · Survival

Select the Small sailing boat and right-click open water within 6 m to launch it. It floats on any water: sea, lakes and all six water types, at their real surface height. To carry it again, look at an unoccupied boat within 6 m and Shift-right-click, with 18 capacity free in your pack. Survival uses up and returns the boat item; creative launches from the catalog without using one.

Right-click open water
Launch the selected boat (Small sailing boat selected, water within 6 m)
Shift + right-click
Pack up the boat you are looking at (unoccupied boat within 6 m, any item held)

A failed launch says 'Boat needs clear water and room for its hull and mast (8 boats maximum)' and uses nothing. Wrecked boats (0 HP) cannot be boarded or packed and are cleared when you next launch (crates/voxelgame-core/src/vehicle/sailing.rs:125-141). Boats are disabled on multiplayer servers ('Boats aren't available on servers yet', game/sailing.rs:49). The recipe belongs to the survival audit and is listed here only for reference.

Sailing: deck, helm, sails, steering and camera

Available

Creative · Survival

Walk or jump onto the boat's wooden deck like normal ground. Press V within 9 m to take the helm, and press V again to step back onto the cockpit. At the helm, hold W to raise the sails and S to reef them, press Space to lower them fully, and steer with A/D. Press C or F5 to switch between first-person and chase view, and hold Alt for free look.

V
Take or leave the helm (within 9 m of the boat or on its deck)
W (hold)
Raise the sail setting; the sails follow over about 2 s (at the helm)
S (hold)
Reef (lower the sail setting) (at the helm)
Space
Lower the sails completely (at the helm)
A / D
Steer left / right (rudder eases in and recentres) (at the helm)
C or F5
Switch first-person / chase camera (at the helm)
Hold Alt
Free look (at the helm)

There is no reverse. The boat can turn while stopped. It stops dead if the hull would run aground or hit another boat, and it can only turn where the new heading still has water under the whole hull (crates/voxelgame-core/src/vehicle/sailing.rs:159-205), so a grounded boat may need packing up and relaunching. Leaving the helm stops the boat immediately. Opening the pack (E) pauses the boat (game.rs:1149).

Sailing: wind, speed and tacking

Available

Creative · Survival

Each world has a fixed prevailing wind direction, and its strength changes with the weather: about 2.8 m/s in clear weather up to 8.5 m/s in thunderstorms. Running with the wind is fastest, and across the wind gives about two-thirds of the wind speed. Within 45 degrees of sailing straight into the wind the sails give no push, so zig-zag (tack) to go upwind. The red masthead pennant and the HUD flag (bow at the top) point downwind.

Because the wind direction never changes in a world, the same routes are always upwind. The HUD bearing 'TO n DEG' is not a compass bearing: 0 deg points to +Z (south on the map) and 90 deg to +X (east) (vehicle_ui.rs:112). Read the flags instead. Seasons do not affect the wind.

Flowing water (placing and blocking water)

Limited

Creative

In creative, the catalog's Water block is a flowing source: it spreads up to 7 half-metre cells sideways and pours down over edges. Any block placed into water displaces it, and digging next to the sea or a lake lets water flow into the gap. Flowing water never recedes. There are no buckets, survival players cannot pick up or place water, and the other five water types are still blocks that do not flow.

Right-click with Water selected
Place a flowing water source (creative)
Right-click with any block aimed into water
Replace that water cell with the block (building)

To get rid of unwanted flowing water, fill each wet cell with blocks. Water from creative building brushes behaves the same way. On a multiplayer server the server runs the water.

Animals, hunting & combat

The 94 animals and how they behave, and hunting with the bow, rifle, rocks and explosives.

Animal drops

Available

Survival

In survival, an animal you kill puts its drops straight into your pack. Meat and venison are food, feathers make arrows, and wool can replace plant fiber; hide currently has no use.

Drops that do not fit are lost (there are no ground items). Killing animals in creative collects nothing. Hunting controls are covered by the combat audit.

Fishing with the Reed fishing rod

Available

Creative · Survival

Craft a Reed fishing rod from 4 boards, 4 Reeds and 2 Plant fiber or Wool, then equip it. Right click open water within 12 m to cast. A bite comes after 2 to 4 seconds and waits until you right click again to reel in 1 Raw meat. Left click cancels the line. Moving more than 16 m from the float, changing the water under it or putting the rod away also cancels it.

Right click (rod equipped)
Cast at open water within 12 m; after a bite, reel in the catch
Left click (rod equipped)
Cancel the line

Source-checked on 2026-11-08 at Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480; no new play test. The rod never wears out and fishing uses nothing up; there is no bait. While it is equipped the rod takes both mouse buttons, so you cannot mine, place blocks or hit animals, and it does nothing at a boat's helm. Lines are never saved. There is no bite sound and the float does not move: the status line and hotbar show the bite. The game's player guide does not describe fishing yet.

Where to fish and what you catch

Available

Creative · Survival

Only open Fresh water, sea Water and Black water take a line; ice, Hot spring water, Boiling water, Dark fjord water and plants in the water do not. Every catch is 1 Raw meat. The fish named depends on the water and biome: carp or trout in fresh water (trout more often in cold and highland biomes), salmon or crab in the sea (crab more often on shallow shores), and always catfish in black water.

Source-checked on 2026-11-08 at Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480; no new play test. The likelier fish comes up about two casts in three. Depth, time of day, weather and season make no difference, and fishing does not take animals out of the water. There is no fish item, bait or rare catch; the game calls its catch tables and wait a first version.

Fishing on a server

Limited

Survival

On a server, including a world you host, fishing works in Survival only and the rod must be in your own pack. Each cast, reel and cancel waits for the server, which uses the same water, wait and catch rules. Only you see your float and line. Creative is refused with 'Fishing on servers requires Survival mode'; other refusals start with 'Fishing refused:'.

Right click (rod equipped, on a server)
Ask the server to cast or reel in
Left click (rod equipped, on a server)
Ask the server to cancel the line

Source-checked on 2026-11-08 at Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480; no new play test. A catch waiting on the line survives a full pack: make room while the rod stays equipped and reel again. Disconnecting, dying or a server restart drops the line. Another of your actions still waiting for the server blocks the rod until it finishes.

Where and how many animals appear

Available

Creative · Survival

Animals appear around you according to the biome: each biome has its own small group of species and every one of the 94 can appear somewhere; swans turn up in wetland fens, flooded grasslands and deltas, and fish only in water deep enough below sea level. Volcanic fields, meteor fields, geyser basins and surface lava tubes have none. Up to 36 wild animals are around you at once (shared by all players on a server), with per-species limits; wild animals more than 180 m away are removed and new ones appear as you explore. Wild animals are not saved; animals you hatched from eggs are.

Source-checked on 2026-11-08 at Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480; no new play test. Land animals spawn only on natural ground, never on planks, bricks, plaster, marble, glass or roof tiles. Spawning waits while you are more than 96 m above or below the ground. Each square gets one try until you have moved roughly 250 m away.

Animal spawn eggs (creative)

Available

Creative

The creative catalog's MOBS tab has a spawn egg for each of the 94 species. Taking one equips it; hold right click to wind up (a full wind-up takes 0.7 s) and release to throw, and the animal hatches where the egg bursts on the first block it hits. Eggs cannot be crafted.

Hold right click, release
Throw the egg; the animal hatches on impact (egg equipped)

Source-checked on 2026-11-08 at Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480; no new play test. A thrown egg is consumed only in survival (if carried there). Hatched animals are saved with the world. When you move more than 180 m away they are set aside, and they return when you come back; a hatched animal that is killed is gone for good. A world keeps at most 64 hatched animals, and an egg cannot hatch while 64 animals are around you ('The egg burst, but nothing could hatch here'). On a server, a refused throw keeps the egg.

Animal behaviour

Available

Any mode

Farm animals stay calm near you; shy wild species (rabbits, foxes, frogs, many birds, horses, zebras, giraffes, big cats, wolves, crocodiles and others) keep about 5 m away (frogs 3 m) and run if you come closer. Any hurt animal bolts for a few seconds. Many animals pause to graze and idle animals turn their heads to watch you. Deer, rabbits, frogs, kangaroos and jerboas bound while fleeing; goats, deer and gazelles jump ledges up to 1 m; otters, penguins and swans swim and fish stay in water.

There is no taming, riding, breeding, feeding, milking or shearing (see animal-taming-breeding).

Creative · Survival

A selected block is shown as a small textured cube gripped in your right hand; tools are held on the right and the bow left of centre with a separate string hand. With nothing in hand, or a block you no longer carry in survival, a bare right arm shows low on the right. Holding left click swings tools, bare hands and held blocks (not bows or rifles), and placing a block plays one swing. A held sailing boat shows no hand.

Owner-requested changes (full-size held block, right-side bow) are planned and not in this snapshot. The visible bare hand, punch/mine/place swing and plain block fist landed in Voxelgame d1def9ef. F1 clean view hides held items.

Available

Settings and sound

Graphics and performance settings, diagnostic overlays and audio.

Shader quality: None, Fast, Cinematic

Available

Any mode

Settings > Graphics > Display > Shader picks the lighting tier. None is plain voxel lighting for weak hardware; Fast (default) adds sun shadows, sun rays and haze; Cinematic refines shadows and rays and adds reflective water, costing extra frame time. Graphics presets also set it.

Source-checked on 2026-11-08 at Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480; no new play test. Cinematic adds per-pixel work in the existing passes rather than extra render targets (settings.rs:361-366). No benchmark or capture was made.

Available

Any mode

Frame limit

Available

Any mode

Settings > Graphics > Display > Frame limit caps rendered frames at 60 (default), 120, 240 or Unlimited. Unlimited removes software frame pacing. There is no separate vsync setting. The FPS box shows the active LIMIT, or UNCAPPED.

Source-checked on 2026-11-08 at Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480; no new play test. The window asks for presentation without vsync where the driver offers it; the frame limit does the pacing. The same limit sets the F3 frame budget (Unlimited uses 60 FPS). No frame-rate measurement was made.

Performance overlay (F3)

Available

Any mode

Press F3 (or use Settings > Advanced > Diagnostics > Performance) to show a CPU-effort pie for the last half second, frame time against your frame budget, the worst recent frame with a spike count, and the lag-spike log status. The budget follows Frame limit (Unlimited uses 60 FPS). Red marks work using more than one CPU core or over half the frame budget. In normal play the GPU box reads “GPU timing unavailable in this view”.

F3
Show/hide the performance overlay (in a world)

Source-checked on 2026-11-08 at Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480; no new play test. A spike is a frame longer than twice the budget and at least 25 ms. While the overlay is open on Linux, spikes are written to lag-spikes.jsonl in $XDG_STATE_HOME/voxelgame or ~/.local/state/voxelgame (src/profiling.rs:49-55). No benchmark was made.

Available

Any mode

Keep the display awake while playing

Limited

Any mode

The native app requests that the desktop stay awake while the game window is focused and visible, including menus and loading. It releases the request on focus loss, hiding, minimization or covering the window. Desktop support varies.

System requirements and supported platforms

Limited

Linux with a Vulkan-capable integrated or discrete GPU and an X11 or XWayland session is the main, tested platform. Installers for Windows 10/11 (64-bit Intel/AMD) and macOS (Apple Silicon or Intel with a Metal GPU) are included but have not yet been checked with real graphics and sound on those systems.

The first build needs internet and several GB of free disk space. README says the 60 FPS target assumes at least an integrated GPU; software Vulkan (llvmpipe) is for diagnostics only (README.md:155-156).

Install on Linux (install.sh)

Available

From the extracted source folder run `bash install.sh` as your normal user. It installs compiler and audio tools (apt-get, dnf or pacman, using sudo only for system packages), Rust stable, builds the game and adds Voxelgame to your application menu. Setup never starts the game or touches existing worlds.

bash install.sh [--yes] [--prefix PATH]…
Run setup; --yes accepts the plan, --prefix changes the app folder, --skip-prerequisites uses tools you installed yourself, --help changes nothing (terminal in the extracted source folder)

Needs internet, several GB free, a working Vulkan driver and X11/XWayland. Other distributions: install the prerequisites listed in docs/INSTALLING.md:69-72 yourself, then use --skip-prerequisites. Fedora gets ffmpeg-free. INSTALLING.md says not to run setup with sudo; the script does not enforce this.

Install on macOS (Install-macOS.command)

Limited

Double-click Install-macOS.command, press Return to accept the plan, finish Apple's Command Line Tools installer if offered, and enter your Mac password if Homebrew asks. Setup installs Homebrew and FFmpeg when needed plus Rust, builds the game for your Mac, and creates Voxelgame.app in your home folder's Applications folder.

Unsigned source installer, not a notarized app: if macOS blocks it use System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway, or run `bash install.sh` in Terminal; do not disable Gatekeeper. Native macOS graphics and audio are untested, and an owner-supplied Metal startup fix is not yet integrated, so the game may fail to start. On some Macs F4 needs Fn+F4. The extracted folder can be deleted after a successful install.

Install on Windows 10/11 (install-windows.cmd)

Limited

Double-click install-windows.cmd, confirm the plan and approve the Microsoft compiler installer if Windows asks. Setup downloads Microsoft C++ Build Tools, Rust and FFmpeg when missing, builds the game and adds Voxelgame to the Start menu. If the compiler setup asks for a restart, restart Windows and run the installer again.

install-windows.ps1 -Yes / -Prefix PATH /…
Same options as the Linux/macOS installer (PowerShell in the extracted folder)

Not validated on a real Windows machine yet. Python, Git and winget are not needed. The Start menu shortcut sets no Voxelgame icon (install-windows.ps1:138-143). Managed PCs may need an administrator to allow scripts.

Where the game, worlds and logs are stored

Available

Installed games keep worlds and settings in a per-user data folder that survives upgrades: Linux ~/.local/share/voxelgame/data, macOS ~/Library/Application Support/Voxelgame, Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\Voxelgame\data. Worlds are in the worlds folder inside it. A source checkout started with./run.sh keeps its worlds in the source folder.

Worlds from a development checkout are not moved automatically; copying the worlds folder into the data folder while the game is closed is the implied manual route (inferred from relative save paths).

Uninstalling

Limited

There is no uninstaller. Delete the app folder and its menu entry (Linux ~/.local/share/applications/voxelgame.desktop, Windows Start menu 'Voxelgame' shortcut). Your worlds stay in the data folder until you delete it yourself.

Rust, Homebrew, compilers and audio tools stay installed. On Windows the FFmpeg copy in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Voxelgame\tools also remains. Deleting the data folder removes all worlds permanently.

Build and run from source (cargo or ./run.sh)

Available

On a prepared Linux machine with Rust 1.75 or newer, run `cargo run --release --locked --bin voxelgame`, or `./run.sh`, which rebuilds only when sources changed and shows a small 'Preparing the game' window while it builds. Started this way, worlds live in the source folder's worlds directory.

Developer route. Optional aplay (alsa-utils) for sound and ffmpeg for music (README.md:153).

Loading screen

Available

Any mode

When the game opens, a tumbling wireframe cube settles into the Voxelgame logo above the current loading stage and an activity bar; later world loads show just the stage and bar. The terrain right around you is prepared before play starts and distant terrain keeps streaming in afterwards.

No percentage is shown; the window stays responsive to resizing and closing.

Available

Any mode

Headless screenshot/benchmark runs can run alongside the open game.

World save files

Available

Any mode

Each world has a .vxw save under worlds. New worlds use worlds/<name>/world.vxw, with a number added on a folder collision; blank or unusable names get world-0001, world-0002 and so on. Separate name, preview and session-history files may sit beside the save. Rename changes its label without moving the save.

Available

Menus

Saving: autosave, F6 and quitting safely

Available

Any mode

F6 saves explicitly and shows 'World saved safely' only after the world file is written, including a hosted world. In a joined world or a --no-save session it writes nothing and says 'This session does not save the world locally'. Main menu, quitting and switching worlds save first; a failed quit-time save keeps the game open. Autosave checks about every 30 seconds. Main menu continues hosting. If a stopped hosted pack needs recovery, F6 retries recovery.

F6
Save now; retry guarded pack recovery when pending
Ctrl+Q / Save & quit / window close
Save and leave before closing; failures keep the session open
Esc > Main menu
Save and show the main menu; hosting continues
Shift+F6
Inspect the explicit recovery choice for a stopped hosted pack

Source-checked on 2026-11-08 at Voxelgame dfeb362ddeca56ff5de77fa26ccdb6e37d05192c; no new play test. A reported failure does not mean the world was saved. Keep the session open, fix the reported error and retry. Walking alone does not make the sparse world dirty; explicit saves include character state. A dedicated server saves its own world and confirms most actions after saving them.

What a world save keeps

Available

Creative · Survival

A save keeps pose, mode, Survival meters, inventory/equipment/hotbar, edits and water/door state, environment controls, home/rest/palette/journal, boats, chest and furniture state (including furniture storage, lamp switches and stove contents with an unfinished batch), milestones, player-hatched animals and dropped item stacks. Procedural wildlife, flying projectiles and primed TNT reset. Display/audio/input preferences are shared separately.

Source-checked on 2026-11-08 at Voxelgame dfeb362ddeca56ff5de77fa26ccdb6e37d05192c; no new play test. Save format 40 includes dropped items and carried-stock records; it did not change in this range. Serialized legacy temperature is inert. Old settings fields remain in .vxw for compatibility. Saving while seated or in a bed needs a clear exit, otherwise it is refused ('Bed exit blocked; cannot save an embedded player').

World controls and shared preferences

Available

Any mode

Mode, terrain generation, time/weather/season controls and progression belong to each world. Display, audio, input and accessibility preferences are shared across worlds through a separate preference file, rather than switching to a save’s old graphics and sound settings. It saves about half a second after a change and on exit.

If it cannot be read, the game keeps it, stops saving preferences for that session and shows “Settings not saved (…)”. Native Windows/macOS profile locations were not checked. Existing .vxw settings fields stay compatible. No native or two-computer playtest.

World size limits

Available

Creative · Survival

Each world file is capped at 8 MiB and 200,000 changed half-metre blocks. From 190,000 changes the game repeats a warning ('saving stops at 200000'), and building refuses changes beyond the budget with 'Save edit budget reached'. A save over 8 MiB is refused and the old file kept. Hosted and dedicated servers also refuse crafting, animal hits, item moves and drops, water exchanges and other actions that would not fit ('… would exceed the save budget or saved state is invalid').

Source-checked on 2026-11-08 at Voxelgame dfeb362ddeca56ff5de77fa26ccdb6e37d05192c; no new play test. Server refusals check the whole prospective save before anything changes: an exact fit is allowed and actions that shrink the save still work. A refused crafting order keeps its ingredients. A refused arrow, rock or egg impact still uses the shot or egg; a refused kill leaves the animal and its drops as they were.

Startup and crash error messages

Limited

Any mode

When the game cannot start, for example with no usable GPU, an unreadable starting world or a mistyped option, it closes and prints the reason to the terminal ('voxelgame failed:...' or 'voxelgame could not start:...'). Menu and desktop launches show no error window, so start the launcher from a terminal to see the message.

Other messages: 'GPU ran out of memory during startup', 'Nearby terrain took too long to prepare; please try again' (shown on the menu), 'audio disabled: playback command unavailable (aplay on Linux; ffplay on Windows/macOS)'. Problems loading other worlds are shown on the main menu instead. Only run.sh shows a dialog, and only for a failed build (run.sh:100-104). Linux launcher path for terminal use: ~/.local/share/voxelgame/app/launch.sh (install.sh:140).

Lag-spike log

Available

Any mode

While the Performance overlay (F3) is on, frames slower than twice your frame budget (at least 25 ms) are recorded with their slowest causes in lag-spikes.jsonl under ~/.local/state/voxelgame (or $XDG_STATE_HOME/voxelgame). Turn F3 off to stop recording.

Entries include world seed, position, frame cost and up to eight contributors, which makes them useful for bug reports. See data-locations for the macOS/Windows path caveats.

Graphics driver and display problems

Limited

On Linux the game needs a working Vulkan driver and an X11 or XWayland session; it has no native Wayland window. It picks your high-performance GPU and falls back automatically to a software renderer such as llvmpipe, which is fine for diagnosis but too slow for normal play.

No in-game GPU diagnostics beyond the F3 overlay. macOS needs a Metal-capable GPU; Windows graphics are not yet validated. Lowering Horizon distance, turning Distant terrain off or choosing Shader None reduces GPU load.

Sound and music requirements

Available

Any mode

Sound effects play through aplay on Linux (alsa-utils) and ffplay on Windows and macOS; music also needs ffmpeg to decode the songs. The installers set these up. Without the player program the game runs silently; without ffmpeg, Music switches itself off and the status line shows 'Music unavailable:...'.

After installing ffmpeg, switch Music back on in Settings > Audio. Song files may be mp3, ogg, wav or flac.

Limited

Any mode

The server owns shared animals, water, supported Survival item/crafting actions and recovery; each player’s inventory stays separate.

Vehicles/boats and some guarded actions stay limited. This does not establish complete multiplayer parity or physical target-device acceptance. Not tested on two computers.

Run a dedicated server (voxelgame-server)

In development

The dedicated server is a separate program that the installers do not build. Built from source, `voxelgame-server --world DIR` hosts a world on 127.0.0.1:27015 by default; for LAN play bind your LAN address, for example --bind 192.168.1.20:27015. Its console accepts /list, /say, /save, /stop and /help. It confirms most player actions only after saving the change.

/list, /say <text>, /save, /stop, /help
List players, broadcast, save now, save and stop, show commands (server console)

Source-checked on 2026-11-08 at Voxelgame dfeb362ddeca56ff5de77fa26ccdb6e37d05192c; no new play test. Other options: --seed, --name, --motd, --mode, --max-players, --autosave-minutes, --no-tui. Refusals arrive at once; a successful craft, meal, drop, placement, storage move, Home action, animal hit, paid shot or respawn waits for the save. A failed write keeps it waiting without repeating it. Developers can test with the scripted bot: cargo run --release -p voxelgame-server --example bot -- HOST:PORT.

Multiplayer menu: Host this world (LAN hosting)

Limited

Host this world hosts the current saved local world and shows its join address. Main menu continues hosting. Stop hosting saves, disconnects players and recovers the owner’s world and pack for solo play. A refused initial save keeps hosting; a stopped-pack recovery error keeps the session guarded for F6 retry or an explicit Shift+F6 choice.

Multiplayer > Host this world / Stop hosting
Start/stop hosting the saved local world
F6
Retry stopped hosted pack recovery
Shift+F6
Inspect final-pack or saved-world-and-pack recovery choice

Source-checked on 2026-11-08 at Voxelgame dfeb362ddeca56ff5de77fa26ccdb6e37d05192c; no new play test. Use a trusted LAN; two-computer acceptance remains incomplete. F6 saves the hosted world. The Creative host can rest and pack up an empty Home (no boards) after pack confirmation. Stopping or saving while seated or in a bed waits for a clear exit. Unresolved recovery blocks ordinary save, world replacement and quit; keep the session open after a failed write. Not tested on two computers.

Headless screenshots and benchmarks (command line)

Developer tool

Advanced: `voxelgame --headless --screenshot=FILE.png` or `--headless --bench=SECONDS` renders offscreen with the normal renderer, without a window, audio or save writes, and can run beside the open game. Benchmarks print one BENCH line with mean, median, 1%-low and worst frame times.

--headless --screenshot=PATH [--screenshot-after=SECS] /…
Capture one PNG or measure frame times, then exit (command line)

Other options: --screen=world|menu|inventory|settings|map, --position=X,Y,Z, --look=YAW,PITCH, --time=cycle|dawn|day|dusk|night|0..1, --weather=..., --shader=none|fast|cinematic, --view-distance=N, --window=WxH, --uncap, --auto-start, --no-save. Works in normal builds but is a developer tool. There is no --profile flag.

02 / WRITING ORDER

The guides players need next.

Practical guides ranked by player need. Each article records its source checks and whether a headless play test was run.

  1. Getting started: your first session Written

    Choose a world, learn the pack and hotbar, and leave with progress saved.

    Covers: Start menu, Creative and survival modes (F4), New worlds: creative by default, survival starter supplies, Walking and looking around, Inventory screen and its tabs, Mouse capture and release, Saving, Main menu and quitting

  2. Controls reference Written

    One verified key table replaces the game README table, which has known mistakes.

    Covers: Walking and looking around, Jumping, Sprinting, Sneaking (ledge guard), Crawling, Swimming and diving, Creative flight, Hold to zoom, Camera perspectives (F5), Ten-slot hotbar, Equipping tools (Tab cycling)

  3. Your first survival day Written

    Survival starts with a small starter pack; players need the shortest safe path to tools, food, water and a respawn point.

    Covers: Health, hunger, thirst and stamina, Eating (R), Drinking and water flasks (T), Mining and collecting blocks, Craft tab (crafting panel), Stone tools (single tier, no durability), Home crate: establish, storage, repair, pack up, Resting and setting your respawn point

  4. Crafting and recipes Written

    All 151 recipes are verified against the game registry; the guide also explains the ingredient groups and cooking on a stove.

    Covers: Craft tab (crafting panel), Complete recipe list, Interchangeable ingredients, Quick craft (X), Charcoal, cooking and glass (no furnace), Glow-crystal recipes in survival

  5. Maps and finding your way home Written

    Players lose builds after travel; markers, journal places and the destination beacon already help.

    Covers: Compact map, Fullscreen world map, Map locator: find biomes and landmarks, Right-click map markers, Journal places and notes, Destinations: map marker, light beacon and on-screen marker, The map in survival (chart only, no fog of war)

  6. Install, update and where your worlds live Written

    Install or update safely, find the last selected world, and keep a separate backup.

    Covers: Install on Linux (install.sh), Install on Windows 10/11 (install-windows.cmd), Install on macOS (Install-macOS.command), Updating an installed game, Where the game, worlds and logs are stored, World save files, Continue resumes the last selected local world

  7. Building basics, furniture and creative tools Written

    Place blocks, make furniture and use brushes and undo while building.

    Covers: Target outline and placement ghost, Placing blocks, Half-metre detail building, Creative brushes (B), Copy brush (copy and paste), Undo and redo building, Build tab and material palettes

  8. Sailing a boat Written

    Wind, tacking and the helm controls are not obvious without a walkthrough.

    Covers: Launching and packing up a sailing boat, Sailing: deck, helm, sails, steering and camera, Sailing: wind, speed and tacking, Boats and saving

  9. Hunting, weapons and animals Written

    Animals never attack; hunting is the renewable food source and the bow and rifle have specific controls.

    Covers: Hitting animals (melee), Alder bow and arrows, Alder rifle and rifle rounds, Throwing rocks, Animal drops, Animal behaviour, Peaceful world: no hostile mobs

  10. Settings and performance Written

    Shader tier, horizon and frame limit decide smoothness on laptops; measured guidance follows in the performance study.

    Covers: Shader quality: None, Fast, Cinematic, Horizon distance, Frame limit, Atmospheric fog (haze) presets, Field of view, Performance overlay (F3)

  11. Fixing startup, sound and save problems Written

    Find errors and logs, protect unreadable saves and recover from failed saves.

    Covers: Startup and crash error messages, When a world cannot be loaded, Graphics driver and display problems, Sound and music requirements, Installer logs, Saving: autosave, F6 and quitting safely

  12. Not in the game yet Written

    One honest page answers the common “is this in the game?” questions without inventing details.

    Covers: Fire, Lava, Natural waterfalls and dripstone caves, Player skins and skin editor

03 / WHERE DOCUMENTS DISAGREE

The code wins.

The audit compared the game’s own README and documents with its code. Where they disagree, this ledger follows the code, and the mismatch is listed here for the game’s maintainers.

  • 17 October update and world-profile follow-up

    The installation guide and its update/world-file entries were refreshed against 36ff7d46073a7f8d0202a1b47b6d7deb580f301b. The remaining feature ledger retains its independently recorded audit baseline. Linux managed-update orchestration is tested; cross-platform parity and both-computer delivery are pending.

    docs/UPDATING.md:1-15 crates/voxelgame-core/src/save.rs:23-31 src/local_startup.rs:55-75

  • Seasonal appearance remains incomplete

    Seasons change palettes without survival penalties or world-content changes. Commit 150cd60 removed the seasonal temperature offset; 35cfc2f8 removes ambient-temperature survival altogether. Seasonal leaf thinning and snowy grass remain planned, without a fresh native visual acceptance claim.

    docs/PHILOSOPHY.md:27 crates/voxelgame-core/src/environment.rs:408-411 crates/voxelgame-core/src/game.rs — 35cfc2f8: ambient-temperature survival removed

  • World list limit and folder names

    The README says the Worlds menu holds 32 worlds and that new worlds get numbered folders. The code lists up to 256 worlds, and a typed world name gets its own folder.

    README.md:661-666 src/worlds.rs:13 src/worlds.rs:208-232

  • Tab and the equipment card

    The README says Tab cycles a 3D equipment card. That card was removed; Tab still cycles carried tools and the status line names the result.

    README.md:601 crates/voxelgame-render/src/hotbar_ui.rs:342-344

  • The Craft-tab filter name

    The game's player guide calls the Craft-tab filter Can craft now. In the game it is an icon button whose tooltip reads 'Ready recipes'; it shows only recipes you can make now, including room for the result.

    docs/PLAYER_GUIDE.md:85-90 crates/voxelgame-core/src/game/inventory_qol/presentation.rs:75 crates/voxelgame-core/src/game/inventory_qol.rs:276-279

  • T at the water’s edge

    The README says T drinks a carried flask. Next to drinkable water, T drinks from the water and refills every empty flask instead.

    README.md:633 crates/voxelgame-core/src/game/consumables.rs:91-110

  • Multiplayer is further along than the README says

    The README says multiplayer is not playable yet. A self-built dedicated server and the --connect option already share movement, building and chat; there is no menu entry and survival damage is not applied.

    README.md:785-786 src/launch.rs:164-166 — --connect/--name options; needs a window src/launch.rs:296-303 — --connect/--name options; needs a window

04 / METHOD & LIMITS

Checked against the source.

5 November guide refresh

Worlds, save recovery, LAN hosting, furniture and settings received a targeted source review at aa136e0103ce5599c6d8a9f70c669dbc758b7357. Refreshed rows record that revision in their notes; other rows retain their earlier evidence. The study timer is outside the current base game, so its old address now links to current guides. No new gameplay session or image capture is claimed.

Dated change history

The game and wiki changelogs group brief player-facing changes by calendar day. Full source narratives, hashes and date receipts remain in the maintenance dataset, outside the Pages artifact. The game review still ends at 5856103c (13 October); wiki history includes the guide refresh through 9017e34 (5 November). This presentation change does not refresh the feature audit or individual game/gallery evidence.

Dated gallery images

Animal portraits were refreshed from game source 9e946731 on 13 October 2026, including Swan. Biome, island and guide images retain their separate capture dates. Responsive previews come from those recorded images, and gallery views open the originals. Studio poses do not demonstrate live animal behavior.

Finding a guide

The home introduces survival and creative play and leads to the biome, animal, item and block catalogs. A shorter shared menu and offline catalog/guide search keep development records out of the main browsing routes. The ten topic indexes and existing URLs remain available. This 13 October 2026 presentation update does not refresh the game audit, article evidence or older biome photographs; fresh biome captures are still pending.

Source, not memory

The audit read an exact export of the audited commit: input handling, menus, crafting, survival, building, world, maps, sailing, combat, platform and settings code. Every feature cites at least one file and line, and the game’s own documents were checked against that code.

Planned means absent

Tracked requests were searched for in the same export. Anything missing, or present only as code that ordinary players cannot reach, is marked Planned or In development, never Available.

Not yet a play test

This ledger records what the code supports. Practical guides add controls and screenshots verified in disposable headless sessions, never a visible game window or a normal player save.

Numbers come from the code

Capacities, ranges, timings and recipe amounts are copied from the constants that define them. When a later game change moves them, the next audit updates this page and its commit.
